prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one floor of an old mine dungeon (timbered galleries dug into a mountain) in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: THE SEVENTH LAYER, the deepest floor of an ancient mine: from the stairs in the north-west a winding gallery of old worn rock with small side niches descends to a square antechamber paved with worn slabs; in its north wall stands a colossal sealed ROCK DOOR of two carved stone slabs (an anvil and a hammer, iron bands); behind it a great rounded hall of ancient dressed stone where a giant armoured guardian of dark riveted iron sits on a throne-dais with a hammer across its knees, and behind the guardian a jagged BREACH in the floor showing only a pale featureless white nothing. Palette: very dark grey and violet-grey stone, iron, pale white in the breach. Ancient, silent, oppressive.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 50 x 42 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2400 x 2016 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, rail, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, colour ramps, level of detail). Do NOT copy anything from it (no objects, signs or buildings from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles, triangles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give cliffs, rock walls, streams and meadows natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- light brown with arcs = the walkable mine FLOOR: packed earth and grey-brown rock of the galleries, cart ruts, small stones and ore crumbs, organic edges (never square or stepped).
- grey-brown with arcs = patches of loose GRAVEL / slag on the floor (walkable, flat).
- brown with steel lines = a RAIL TRACK for mine carts (walkable): dark wooden sleepers, two steel rails.
- brown with plank lines = TIMBER PLANKS: a boardwalk or a bridge of beams over a drop (walkable deck).
- teal = underground WATER (not walkable): dark still water with faint reflections.
- black = a deep CHASM / shaft (not walkable): a sheer drop into darkness.
- grey circles = BOULDERS, heaps of ore and rubble (not walkable).
- brown with vertical lines = TIMBER structures (not walkable): heavy wooden beams and props, scaffolds, sheds.
- very dark grey = solid ROCK (not walkable): the mountain's rock around the galleries, dark and jagged, seen from above, the sheer faces showing where it rises above the floor, streaked with ore veins; the gallery walls are shored with timber frames here and there; the outlines are natural and rounded, NEVER square, stepped or staircase-shaped; everything outside the floors is solid rock.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(84,80,90) = the great ROCK DOOR of the seventh layer: two huge slabs of dark stone carved with an anvil and a hammer, iron bands, sealed shut.
- the blocks in colour rgb(140,130,116) = a short passage of worn stone slabs leading to the back of the rock door.
- the blocks in colour rgb(70,72,80) = the IRON GUARDIAN: a giant armoured figure of dark riveted iron, seated on a stone throne-dais with a great hammer across its knees, head bowed.
- the blocks in colour rgb(236,236,240) = the BREACH: a jagged oval hole broken through the floor, and inside it no rock and no darkness, only a pale featureless WHITE (no bottom, no detail).
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates, carts or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, mine carts on the rails, treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.

Render entire image edge-to-edge without text/UI. Preserve exact guide geometry: solid dark violet-charcoal rocky mountain background; a northwest upper winding mine gallery starts in the upper-left at x~240-575 y~140-350, curves down x~290-480 toward a western small chamber x~90-450 y~570-810, a narrow winding descending passage from x~240-430 y~770-1230, then winding diagonally southeast to a broad antechamber x~1060-1680 y~1490-1850; side niche extending east x~400-800 y~1000-1200; antechamber immediately south of the large square sealed rock door at x~1200-1490 y~1340-1490. Ancient silent oppressive mine, neutral soft even albedo lighting (not night), very dark warm grey and violet-grey rock, iron, pale white breach. Premium crisp hand-placed SQUARE-pixel clusters, hue-shifted ramps and dark warm outlines, organic crags, rich natural geological texture matched to second attached image. RPG top-down slight 3/4 view but no isometric/perspective/3D; no anti-alias, painterly marks, noise or blur. No characters other than specifically requested iron statue guardian; no text, rails unless shown, carts, lanterns, signs, glow, borders, grids, vignette.
